items.title: Toward verifiably private learning from federated data
items.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) allows devices with private data to collaborate in training a shared model. We present a next-generation FL system based on Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) that addresses operational challenges associated with earlier systems and provides externally verifiable central Differential Privacy (DP) guarantees for the first time while offering a better privacy-utility tradeoff. In our system, devices upload data encrypted with keys managed by a TEE-hosted Key Management Service (KMS). The uploaded data is cryptographically tied to a policy limiting the set of Python programs that may later process the data in server-side TEEs. External parties may inspect public transparency logs to observe the set of workloads allowed by these policies. Our experimental results show that the new system improves device coverage and favorably shifts privacy-utility curves by enabling collected data to be integrated into the server-side workload at a schedule that optimizes DP guarantees and is unaffected by device availability. Our new system has been productionized, enabling models for the Android Keyboard (Gboard) to be trained faster and achieve better accuracy under smaller, now externally verifiable privacy budgets in comparison to models trained using the prior system.

items.llm_tldr_en: Federated learning lets devices with private data jointly train a shared model, but earlier systems struggle to give externally verifiable privacy guarantees. This paper presents a next-generation FL system based on Trusted Execution Environments: devices upload data encrypted with TEE-managed keys, cryptographically tied to policies limiting processing programs. It provides the first externally verifiable central differential privacy guarantees with a better privacy-utility tradeoff, aided by public transparency logs.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 联邦学习允许多方在私有数据上协作训练共享模型，但既有系统在隐私保证的可验证性与隐私-效用权衡上仍有不足。本文提出基于可信执行环境的下一代联邦学习系统，设备上传由TEE托管KMS密钥加密的数据，并以密码学方式绑定限制处理程序。系统首次提供可外部验证的中心化差分隐私保证，同时取得更好的隐私-效用权衡，并通过公开透明日志供外部审计，推动联邦学习走向可验证隐私与可靠落地。

items.title: AgentWorld: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Collaboration of Multi-agent LLMs
items.abstract: Existing multi-agent benchmarks primarily test in competitive settings, short-horizon interactions under 20 steps, or simply aggregate individual performance, failing to isolate and highlight genuine collaboration capabilities of LLM-based agents. We introduce AgentWorld, a benchmark of 100 human-annotated tasks (with 100 augmented variants) for evaluating long-horizon, multi-agent collaboration. Tasks span 50+ interaction rounds across a rich MMORPG sandbox and require 3-20 agents with asymmetric roles and abilities to coordinate through communication, joint planning, and resource sharing under a blackbox setting where each agent acts independently without access to others' internal states. To quantify collaboration effectiveness in addition to conventional binary task success, we propose Causal Collaboration Effectiveness (CCE), a graph-based metric that traces causal dependencies between agent actions and measures what fraction of a team's effort actually contributed to the outcome. Experiments with Gemini 3 Flash, Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5 Mini, and DeepSeek R1-70B show that even the best model achieves only 52.0% task success, with systematic failure modes including communication breakdowns, role confusion, and inability to maintain shared plans across rounds. AgentWorld is fully open-source.

items.llm_tldr_en: Existing multi-agent benchmarks test competitive, short-horizon interactions or merely aggregate individual scores, failing to isolate genuine collaboration. This paper introduces AgentWorld, 100 human-annotated long-horizon tasks in an MMORPG sandbox requiring 3-20 agents to coordinate under a blackbox setting.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 现有多智能体基准多测试竞争性、二十步以内的短时程交互，或仅汇总个体表现，难以隔离并凸显真正的协作能力。本文提出AgentWorld基准，包含100个经人工标注的长时程协作任务及100个增强变体，在大型多人在线沙盒中跨越50多轮交互，要求3至20个能力与角色不对称的智能体在黑盒条件下通过通信、联合规划与资源共享协作。该基准为量化多智能体协作效能提供了新工具。
